title: Lesson 1: Loving God
description: The Father runs toward you first. This lesson introduces the Greatest Commandment, which begins with God's love: receive His love, then give your whole self back to Him and out to others.

courseLogo.title: Welcome to Growing Deep

blocks.text: In the 101 Starting Course, you took your first steps with Jesus. Now you begin three Growing courses: Growing Deep (201), Growing Up (202), and Growing Out (203). Growing Deep begins with your most important relationship, the one between you and God, and it begins with a father on a road.

blocks.alt: A father running down the road toward his returning son until he reaches him

blocks.title: The Running Father
blocks.text:
Jesus once told a story about a father and his two sons. Most people know it as the Parable of the Prodigal Son, but watch the father first.

The younger son asked for his inheritance early, which was like saying, "I wish you were dead." Then he left home and wasted everything. When he finally came to himself, he started back with a speech ready, hoping to be treated like a servant.

"But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt compassion, and ran and embraced him and kissed him." (Luke 15:20)

The father did not wait for the speech. He ran. He embraced him. He kissed him. Then came the robe, the ring, and the feast. Before the son could earn anything back, the father welcomed him home.

This is the heart of God toward you. Not patient tolerance. Not cautious acceptance. A Father running to bring His child home.

Hold on to the image of that robe the father wrapped around his son. It is more than welcome-home clothing. It is a picture of something Jesus was about to do, and you will come back to it in the next lesson.
1.1 - When you picture the Father running toward you before you have cleaned yourself up, how does that affect you?
Because He Loved First

The title of this lesson carries a double meaning, and both sides matter. God is a loving God who pursues you, and loving God back is what you were made to do. His love comes down first. Your love for Him, and for others, is love you first received.

So when Jesus was asked what matters most in all of life, He did not answer with a philosophy or a program. He went back to the oldest prayer in Israel, the words faithful families had prayed morning and evening for a thousand years. It is called the Shema (pronounced "sheh-MAH"), and it means "hear."

Jesus answered, "The most important is, 'Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.'"

Heart, soul, mind, and strength are not four separate compartments. They are four ways of saying your whole self. Your deepest desires, the core of who you are, your thoughts, your energy, all of it. Nothing held back. It is the highest command Jesus ever gave, and if you are honest it sounds impossible. How do you love anyone that completely, let alone an invisible God?
Here is the part that changes everything. You do not have to generate this kind of love from nothing.
We love because he first loved us.

This is the confession the whole Christian life swings on: I do not love God to make Him love me. I love God because He loved me first. Every morning, every act of obedience, every return from drifting begins there.

This is the simple rhythm of the Christian life: receive from God, and give to others. First, you receive the Father's love. Then you give it away, back to Him in love and out to the people around you. What you receive, you give away.

When that love comes down and lands in your heart, it does not stay there. It moves. That love has a shape: it comes from God to you, it returns from you to Him, and it overflows from you to the people around you.

This is the Greatest Commandment, and it is shaped like a cross for a reason. The vertical beam is the love between God and you, His love coming down and your love going back up. The horizontal beam is where that love overflows to the people God has placed near you, and it reaches in two directions. In Growing Up (202), you will follow one arm home, learning what it means to belong and to love your family and your church family. In Growing Out (203), you will follow the other arm to people who do not yet follow Jesus. But you cannot reach out until you have first received, so Growing Deep starts here.

That is very different from the way many people picture God. A boss watches your work and measures your performance. A father watches the road and longs for you to come home. If you see God mainly as a boss, obedience will feel like proving yourself. If you receive Him as Father, obedience becomes a grateful response to the One who already called you His child. Jesus said, "If you love me, you will keep my commandments" (John 14:15). Love comes first, and obedience follows.
1.2 - How would your obedience this week look different if it came from gratitude instead of fear?
1.3 - Where do you feel most stuck right now: receiving God's love, loving Him back, or loving the people around you?

One last word before this first lesson closes. The Father who runs is also the Father who gives. He did not only run down a dusty road. He gave the most precious thing He had so the road home would exist at all.
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.

There is one God in three Persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This is called the Trinity. The Father, the Creator of the universe, loves you. The Son saves you. The Spirit fills you. The next two lessons turn to the Son who made the road home possible and the Spirit who lives inside you. These three lessons belong together, and this week is where you plant the root.
This Week's Practice

Each morning this week, before you check your phone, start with this truth: I do not love God to make Him love me. I love God because He loved me first. And sometime this week, read the full story in Luke 15:11-32.
Lesson 1 Review

God loved you before you ever loved Him back. The whole Christian life begins there: receive His love, then give your whole self to Him and to others. You do not love God to make Him love you. You love God because He loved you first.
In the next lesson, you will see what the Father does when His child comes home: He reaches for the robe.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
